descriptions.home: See this month's figures and what to do next.
descriptions.transactions: Record sales and payments. Switch between quick entry, the journal grid and compound entries; all of them produce the same journal entries.
descriptions.inbox: Review candidates made from receipt photos and card or bank statements, and record them. Nothing goes into your books until you record it.
descriptions.ledgers: View the journal, general ledger, cash and bank books, expense book, and receivables and payables by partner, and save them as CSV or PDF.
descriptions.reports: See the trial balance and account balances. Every figure is calculated from your journal entries.
descriptions.receivables: Manage recurring sales such as tuition and membership fees, and their payments.
descriptions.closing: Finish opening balances, depreciation and inventory, and get the figures for the blue-return statement. This is also where you find the values for your income and consumption tax returns, and carry balances forward to the next year.
descriptions.master: Manage accounts, descriptions, partners and business-use split rules.
descriptions.data: Back up and restore your books, bring in books from Excel or CSV, save them as CSV or PDF, and see the change history.
descriptions.settings: Use the descriptions under the headings to find a setting. For payment details on documents, open Documents and email. For filing reminders, open Business details and tax filing.
descriptions.help: How to use the app and what the accounting terms mean, for first-time users.
descriptions.documents: Create invoices, estimates, delivery notes and receipts, and send them as PDF or by email. Invoices connect to recording sales and payments.

setup.title: Getting started
setup.intro: Set up your books in four steps. You can change these later in Settings.
setup.businessDescription: The person filing the return and the business name.
setup.industryHint: Optional. e.g. English school, design, retail
setup.invoiceRegistrationNoHint: If registered, enter the number on your registration notice (T followed by 13 digits). Leave this blank if you have not registered.
setup.invoiceRegistrationNoLookup: Check a number on the National Tax Agency website
setup.filingDescription: If unsure, choose the blue return (650,000 yen deduction). Without the blue return application, choose the white return.
setup.taxDescription: For the year you are setting up, choose Tax-exempt if you are exempt from consumption tax. If you are a taxable business, choose the calculation method you use for your return.
setup.taxHelpTitle: How to check your consumption tax status
setup.taxHelpExempt: You are generally tax-exempt if your taxable sales two years ago were 10 million yen or less and you have not registered for invoices. Other criteria, such as sales in the first half of the previous year or electing to be taxable, can make you taxable. You are taxable during your invoice registration period.
setup.taxHelpReturn: If you already filed for the year, check your copy of that year's consumption tax return. If you filed through e-Tax, you can view your return from the receipt notice in your message box.
setup.taxHelpSimplified: A return labeled 簡易課税用 (simplified method) means you filed using the simplified method.
setup.taxHelpStandard: On a return labeled 一般用 (general use), a mark in the 20% special rule box means you used that rule. If you did not apply a special rule, you used the general method.
setup.taxHelpNotification: The simplified method generally requires an advance election and must be kept for at least two years after it takes effect. If you have yet to file for the year, check your copy of the election notice for its effective date. If you are unsure about your election or tax status for the year, ask your local tax office or a tax accountant.
setup.exemptWithInvoiceNo: Once you register for invoices, you are taxable from the registration date and need to file a consumption tax return. If your registration covers any part of the year you are setting up, choose one of the taxable options. If you became taxable because you registered, you may be able to use the 20% special rule.
setup.yearDescription: Choose the year you start your books. A sole proprietor's year runs from January to December.
setup.templateBody: Standard accounts that match the blue return statement (cash, sales, supplies and so on) are added, plus accounts and home-use split rules common in your business. On the Master data screen, you can add or rename accounts and adjust the percentage splits to reflect your actual business use.
setup.template_schoolHint: Teaching materials, training and more. Home-classroom split
setup.template_serviceHint: Fees, meetings, vehicle and more. Home-office split
setup.template_retailHint: Sales promotion, packaging and more. Shop-and-home split
setup.template_restaurantHint: Sanitation, packaging and more. Shop-and-home split
setup.template_constructionHint: Tool rental, waste disposal and more. Vehicle and phone splits
setup.template_beautyHint: Treatment supplies, laundry and more. Shop-and-home split
setup.template_itWebHint: Software, hosting and more. Home-office split
setup.template_deliveryHint: Fuel, road tolls and more. Vehicle and phone splits

master.search: Search by code, name or kana
master.empty: Nothing registered yet. Use "Add" to register one.
master.codeHint: Letters and digits. Used when typing entries by number
master.name: Name
master.nameEnHint: Optional. Shown when the language is English
master.categoryLocked: The category of a standard account cannot be changed
master.allocationRuleHint: Optional. Splits payments into business and personal parts
master.parentAccountHint: e.g. one sub-account per bank account under Ordinary deposits
master.businessPercentHint: An integer from 0 to 100. Use records such as business floor area or usage time.
master.paymentAccountHint: Cash, bank accounts, card payables and so on. Shown in quick entry and in account balances
master.billingNameHint: Name printed on invoices, including honorifics such as 御中 or 様. If empty, the name is used.

journal.simpleDescription: Record money coming in and going out without bookkeeping terms. It is saved as a journal entry.
journal.gridDescription: Enter one journal entry per row. Find accounts by code or part of the name. Press Enter to move to the next field; Enter on the last field saves the row.
journal.compoundDescription: Enter transactions with several debit or credit lines (wages and withholding tax, sales and fees, loan repayment and interest, and so on).
journal.owner_draw: Business money used or withdrawn for personal use
journal.owner_contribution: Moved personal money into a business account
journal.memoHint: Optional. What you bought, for example
journal.noPaymentAccounts: There are no money accounts. On the Master data screen, mark cash or bank accounts as "Use as a money account".
journal.amountOutOfRange: Enter a whole number of 1 yen or more.
journal.carryOver: After saving, keep the same accounts for the next row
journal.emptyMonth: No entries for this month yet. Type into the row of the table to add one.
journal.unbalanced: Debits and credits do not match
journal.compoundSaveHint: You can save once the debit total equals the credit total.
journal.allocationTitle: Business-use split (only the business share is an expense)
journal.allocate: Count only the business share as an expense and the rest as personal (owner's drawings)
journal.businessPercentHint: An integer from 0 to 100. Use records such as business floor area or usage time.
journal.depositTargetHint: Choose it if this is a payment for an invoice or a recurring sale. It clears the receivable or records the payment for that month.
journal.purposeIncomplete: Set the debit and credit accounts in Master to use this description.
journal.amountInvalid: Enter a whole amount of at least 1 yen.
journal.contentRequired: Choose the account that describes the transaction.
journal.paymentRequired: Choose the account the money went into or came out of.
journal.personalPayment: I paid with personal funds or a personal card
journal.personalPaymentHint: Records the business expense against owner contributions. If you split the expense, only the business portion is recorded.
journal.unpaidIncome: The customer has not paid yet
journal.unpaidIncomeHint: Use this for sales invoiced outside Chobiyori. When paid, choose Accounts Receivable under Income. For a Chobiyori invoice, record the sale from the issued invoice.
journal.entryNotFound: This transaction could not be found.

reports.openingNote: The balances at the start of the year are the ones entered under "Opening balances" on the Year-end screen. Until you enter them, they are treated as 0.
reports.unbalanced: Debits and credits do not match. Check your journal entries.
reports.preTaxIncome: Income before the blue return deduction
reports.preTaxIncomeHint: Revenue − cost of sales − expenses, from the start of the year to the end month.
reports.empty: No entries in this period yet. Record them on the Transactions screen.
reports.noPaymentAccounts: There are no money accounts. On the Master data screen, mark cash or bank accounts as "Use as a money account".
reports.negativeBalanceHint: An account has a negative balance. Check for missing entries or payments recorded against the wrong account.

errors.tooLong: This is too long. Please shorten it.
errors.duplicateCode: This code is already used. Please choose another.
errors.notFound: It could not be found. Please reopen the screen.
errors.inUse: It is in use, so it cannot be deleted or recategorized. Deactivate it if you no longer need it.
errors.systemAccount: Standard accounts cannot be deleted or recategorized. Deactivate it if you no longer need it.
errors.inactive: This item is deactivated. Activate it on the Master data screen, or choose another one.
errors.unbalanced: The debit total and the credit total differ. Check the amounts.
errors.sameAccount: The same account is on both the debit and the credit side. Choose a different account.
errors.yearClosed: The books for a closed year cannot be changed.
errors.database: Could not read or write your books. Please restart the app.
errors.notInTauri: Only the screens are shown in the browser. Your books are available when you run the app.
errors.unknown: Something went wrong. Please try again.
errors.unencodable: Some characters (such as emoji) cannot be written in Shift_JIS. Save with UTF-8 instead.

errors.fileWrite: The file could not be saved. Try a different folder.
errors.tooManyStatementRows: The statement exceeds 100,000 rows. Split the file before importing it.
errors.smallAssetIneligible: The filing type or acquisition date is ineligible for the small-asset rule.
errors.smallAssetLimit: This would exceed the annual 3 million yen limit for the small-asset rule.
errors.importBlocked: Nothing was imported because some rows still need fixing. Fix the rows in the list, then choose the file again.
errors.alreadyRecorded: This month has already been recorded or skipped. Reopen the screen.
errors.secretStore: The place where the API key is kept (Windows Credential Manager or Mac Keychain) could not be used. Sign in to your computer again and try again.
errors.noApiKey: To read receipts, register an API key under "Receipt reading" in Settings. Until then, you can type the details while looking at the image.
errors.badApiKey: The API key is wrong or no longer works. Check the key in Google AI Studio and register it again.
errors.offline: Could not reach the reading service. Once you are online, press Read. The receipts are still waiting.
errors.rateLimited: The reading limit was reached. Wait a while and try again.
errors.modelNotFound: The model in Settings was not found. The name may be wrong, or the model may have been retired. Check the model name under "Receipt reading" in Settings. The receipts are still waiting.
errors.quotaExhausted: Today's reading limit was reached, or the model in Settings is not available on the free tier. Press Read again tomorrow, or change the model under "Receipt reading" in Settings. The receipts are still waiting.
errors.readFailed: The receipt could not be read. Type the details while looking at the image.
errors.consentRequired: Before sending receipt images, read where they go and agree under "Receipt reading" in Settings.
errors.openingConfirmed: Opening balances are already confirmed. Press "Undo confirmation" first, then make your changes.
errors.monthLocked: This month is closed, so entries can't be added or changed. To change it, reopen the month under Year-end > Close.
errors.wrongPassword: The password is wrong. Check upper and lower case and the input language, then try again.
errors.invalidRecoveryCode: This recovery code can't be used. Check the most recent code issued for these books.
errors.samePassword: Choose a password different from your current one.
errors.weakPassword: The password is too short. Use 8 or more characters.
errors.booksLocked: Your books aren't open yet. Restart the app and enter your password.
errors.backupInvalid: This file can't be restored. Check the password used when the backup was made, or choose another backup.
errors.documentIssued: An issued document can't be changed. To correct it, press "Cancel document" and make a new one.
errors.linkedPosting: This entry is linked to an invoice or recurring sale. To change its accounts or partner, recreate it from the original record.

errors.mailFailed: The email couldn't be sent. Check your internet connection, the recipient address and the server settings. You can also send it with "Open draft".
errors.monthInvoiced: This month is billed by an invoice. Record the payment as a payment for the invoice.
errors.invalidDate: Check the date. Days that don't exist (such as November 31) can't be entered.
errors.invalidCode: Use only letters and digits for the code.
errors.invalidRegistrationNo: Enter the registration number as T followed by 13 digits.
errors.calendarCancelled: Calendar connection was cancelled or timed out.

receiptSettings.title: Receipt reading
receiptSettings.description: Receipt photos are sent to Google's Gemini (AI) to read the date, amount and shop. To use it, create an "API key" (a kind of password) with your own Google account and register it here.
receiptSettings.guideTitle: How to get an API key
receiptSettings.step1: Have a Google account ready. A Gmail account is fine.
receiptSettings.step2: Open Google AI Studio (the URL below) in your browser and sign in with your Google account. Press "Create API key" to make a key (Google sets up what is needed automatically). Copy the key.
receiptSettings.step2Hint: Copy the URL and paste it into the browser you normally use.
receiptSettings.step3: Paste the key into the "API key" field below and register it. The key is kept in this computer's credential store (Windows Credential Manager or Mac Keychain) and is never shown again.
receiptSettings.noteLimits: It is free to use, but there are limits per day and per minute. A person's usual receipts normally fit. If the limit is reached, reading continues after a short wait.
receiptSettings.noteFreeTier: While you use it for free, the images you send may be used by Google to improve its services.
receiptSettings.notePaid: If you set up billing (paid) in Google AI Studio, the images are no longer used to improve services. The cost is expected to be under 1 yen per receipt, but prices and terms change, so check Google's latest information.
receiptSettings.noteLeak: If someone may have learned your key, delete it in Google AI Studio, make a new one and register it again.
receiptSettings.noteData: Only the receipt image is sent. Your books, partners and customer names are not sent; they stay on this computer.
receiptSettings.consentTitle: Where images go, and your agreement
receiptSettings.consentWhere: Receipt images are sent to Google's Gemini API (Google AI Studio) to be read.
receiptSettings.consentWhat: Only the receipt image is sent. For receipts with a name on them, choose "Don't send" in the inbox and type the details yourself.
receiptSettings.consentFreeTier: While you use it for free, the images you send may be used by Google to improve its services.
receiptSettings.consent: I have read the above and agree to send receipt images
receiptSettings.keyNotSet: No API key is registered yet.
receiptSettings.apiKeyHint: Paste the key you copied from Google AI Studio. A registered key is never shown.
receiptSettings.cardAccount: When paid by card or e-money
receiptSettings.modelHint: You normally don't need to change this. Change it if Google retires the model.

closing.openingHint: Enter the cash, deposits and other assets you had at the start of the year, debts such as loans, and the owner's capital. You can confirm once total assets equal total liabilities and capital. From the second year these are filled in by "Carry forward".
closing.openingConfirmed: Opening balances are confirmed. To change them, press "Undo confirmation".
closing.openingAmount: Balance at the start of the year
closing.openingAmountFor: Balance of {name} at the start of the year
closing.openingBalanced: Total assets equal total liabilities and capital
closing.openingDifference: The totals differ by {amount} yen. The difference is often settled with the owner's capital.
closing.openingSaveFirst: After changing amounts, press "Save" before confirming.
closing.assetsHint: Register machines, computers, vehicles and the like costing 100,000 yen or more, and the app works out this year's depreciation (the part you count as an expense each year). Nothing goes into the books until you press "Record".
closing.assetsEmpty: No fixed assets yet. Use "Add a fixed asset" to register one.
closing.assetsTitle: Fixed assets and this year's depreciation
closing.methodHint_straight_line: The same amount each year. This is the usual method for sole proprietors.
closing.methodHint_declining_balance: More in the early years. Requires notifying the tax office.
closing.methodHint_lump_sum: Items under 200,000 yen, in equal parts over 3 years.
closing.methodHint_small_asset: Eligible blue-return filers can expense assets in the acquisition year, subject to the acquisition-date threshold and a 3 million yen annual limit.
closing.assetInUse: Depreciation has been recorded, so it cannot be deleted. If you sold or discarded it, enter the date you let it go.
closing.smallAssetTotal: Assets registered under the small-asset rule this year: {total} yen (limit {limit} yen)
closing.depreciationNote: The business share becomes depreciation expense and the rest goes to owner's drawings. Check useful lives and methods with a tax accountant or the tax office.
closing.acquiredOnHint: The date you started using it for the business. Depreciation is counted by month from then.
closing.usefulLifeHint: The number of years set by law. You can pick from the examples below.
closing.businessPercentHint: An integer from 0 to 100. Use records such as business floor area or usage time.
closing.disposedOnHint: Enter if you sold or discarded it. Depreciation runs until that month.
closing.laterStart: I started keeping these books after the year I bought it
closing.bookValue: Book value at the start of that year
closing.bookValueHint: Enter the year-end book value from last year's statement.
closing.inventoryHint: Enter the value of goods and materials left unsold at year end, and the app works out the cost of sales and records it. If you don't buy goods for resale, you can skip this.
closing.inventoryOpening: Inventory at the start of the year
closing.costOfSalesFormula: Cost of sales = inventory at the start + purchases − inventory at year end
closing.inventoryClosingInputHint: The total of goods left on December 31, valued at what you paid for them.
closing.inventoryRecorded: Inventory is recorded in the books.
closing.checklistHint: Things to do at year end ({done} / {total} done). Items the books can tell are ticked automatically.
closing.checkHint_opening: Enter and confirm them on the "Opening balances" tab.
closing.checkHint_accruals: Record sales and payments that cross the year (such as December's paid in January) in the year they belong to.
closing.checkHint_allocation: Check that the business share of rent, utilities and the like for a home office is right.
closing.checkHint_depreciation: Record it on the "Fixed assets and depreciation" tab.
closing.checkHint_inventory: Enter the year-end inventory on the "Inventory" tab.
closing.check_badDebt: Consider an allowance for bad debts
closing.checkHint_badDebt: For receivables that may not be collected. Ask a tax accountant whether to use it.
closing.checkHint_cashCount: Check that cash on hand and your bankbook on December 31 match the books.
closing.checkHint_owner: Check that private money in and out is recorded as owner's drawings or contributions.
closing.carryHint: Create the opening balances for {next} from this year's closing balances.
closing.carryAssets: Cash, deposits, assets and liabilities carry over at their year-end balances.
closing.carryOwner: Owner's drawings and contributions start at 0.
closing.carryCapital: Owner's capital becomes: year-end capital + income before the blue-return deduction + owner's contributions − owner's drawings.
closing.carryOverwrite: The next year has saved opening balances. Check the box to replace them.
closing.carryDone: Created the opening balances for {year} (owner's capital {capital} yen).
closing.carryDoneCreated: Created FY {year} and its opening balances (owner's capital {capital} yen).
closing.statementHint: Figures to copy into the blue-return statement (general), in the order of its boxes. Everything is calculated from the books.
closing.taxAccountantNote: Form fields and deductions can change. Compare the NTA form and guide for the filing year with your records.
closing.statementOk: Assets equal liabilities and capital, and the income matches
closing.issue_openingUnbalanced: Opening assets do not equal opening liabilities and capital. Fix them on the "Opening balances" tab.
closing.issue_closingUnbalanced: Year-end assets do not equal liabilities and capital. Check the opening balances and entries.
closing.issue_incomeMismatch: The income on the profit and loss statement does not match the books. Check for accounts not mapped to a statement line.
closing.issue_expensesMerged: {value} expense accounts did not fit in the blank boxes and were added to miscellaneous expenses.
closing.issue_ownerOpening: Owner's drawings or contributions have a balance at the start of the year. Set them to 0 and include them in owner's capital.
closing.issue_whiteFiling: Family employee salaries have been excluded from expenses for this white return. Check the separate family worker deduction.
closing.deductionHint: The 650,000 yen deduction requires filing via e-Tax or keeping qualifying electronic books; otherwise it is 550,000 yen. The deduction never exceeds the income.
closing.whiteHint: Amounts for the white-return income and expense statement. If eligible, enter your confirmed family worker deduction below.
closing.whiteDeductionHint: Check NTA No.2075: a relative sharing your livelihood, age 15 or older at year end, working exclusively in the business for over six months. Per worker, use the lower of JPY 860,000 for a spouse (500,000 for another relative) and income before deduction divided by (worker count + 1). Enter the total. These workers cannot also qualify as a dependent or deductible spouse. Enter 0 if ineligible. Worker counts and eligibility are not assessed automatically.
closing.issue_whiteDeductionExceedsIncome: The saved family worker deduction exceeds current income before deduction. Recalculate it after transaction changes and save the revised amount.
closing.issue_negativeBalance: Some lines have a negative year-end balance ({value}). Check for missing entries for fixed assets or loans (such as the payment for an asset you bought) and for entries in the wrong account.
closing.assetPurchaseNote: To record the payment for an asset, choose "Payment for the purchase" when you register it, or record it on the Transactions screen (for example, Tools and equipment / Ordinary deposits).
closing.purchasePaymentHint: Choose the account you paid from to also record the purchase (asset / account) on the date first used. If you paid with personal money, choose Owner's contributions.

security.createTitle: Choose a password for your books
security.createDescription: Your books are kept on this PC, locked with a password. You'll enter it each time you start the app.
security.encryptTitle: Add a password to your books
security.encryptDescription: From this version, your books are locked with a password. Choose one and your current books will be locked. Everything in them stays.
security.unlockDescription: Your password is needed to open your books.
security.forgetWarning: After opening your books, generate a recovery code in Settings and keep it somewhere safe.
security.resetDescription: Use the recovery code you generated in Settings. Generate a new code after resetting your password. Previous backups still need the password used to create them.
security.recoveryDescription: Generate a code you can use to open these books if you forget your password.
security.replaceRecoveryCode: Generating a new code invalidates the previous one.
security.keepRecoveryCode: This code is shown only once. Save it somewhere safe, such as a password manager.
security.passwordHint: {min} or more characters. Don't reuse one from elsewhere.
security.mismatch: The two passwords don't match. Enter the same one twice.
security.changeDescription: Change the password you enter when starting the app.
security.changeBackupNote: Backups made before the change open with the old password. Keep a note of the old one too.
security.changeDeviceNote: Verify with Windows Hello / Touch ID when you change your password to keep device login enabled.
security.changeDeviceFailed: Device authentication was incomplete, so the password change was canceled. Try again.
security.changed: Password changed. Use the new password when opening your books with a password. Generate a new recovery code if you use one.
security.linkedUnlockDescription: Authenticate with Windows Hello / Touch ID, or open with your password.
security.deviceTitle: Open with Windows Hello / Touch ID
security.deviceDescription: Set up with your books password and device authentication. Once enabled, Windows Hello / Touch ID can open your books at startup, even offline.
security.deviceAuthenticationHint: Follow the Windows Hello / Touch ID prompt to verify your identity.
security.deviceOpen: Open with Windows Hello / Touch ID
security.deviceNote: Resetting your password with a recovery code or restoring a backup removes device login on this PC.
security.lockedOut: Locked after too many wrong passwords ({time} left).
security.attemptsLeft: {count} more wrong attempts will lock input.

backup.title: Backup and restore
backup.description: Your whole books (including receipt images) are saved in one file, locked with the same password. When you close the app, a backup is made if anything changed, and the latest 7 are kept. Nothing is sent off this PC.
backup.restorePasswordNote: To restore a backup, use the password your books had when it was made.
backup.sizeNote: In case this PC breaks, set the folder to a USB stick or external disk, or copy the backups now and then. Many images make backups larger.
backup.backupPassword: Password used when the backup was made
backup.backupPasswordHint: After restoring, your books open with your current password.
backup.restoreWarning: Your current books will be replaced with this backup. A backup of the current books is made first.

history.title: Change history
history.description: Entries added, changed or deleted in FY {year}, and actions like closing and restoring, newest first.
history.searchPlaceholder: Entry date (YYYY-MM-DD), memo or document number
history.invalidRange: Check the start and end times. The end must be at or after the start.
history.documentSent: Recorded that a document was sent
history.invoiceRegistrationSaved: Saved the invoice registration number and date
history.whiteDeductionSaved: Saved the family worker deduction as {amount} yen
history.filingTypeChanged: Changed the filing type for FY {year}
history.taxStatusChanged: Changed the consumption tax status for FY {year}

locks.description: Close a month once you've checked it, and its entries can't be added or changed from any screen. Closing a month also closes the months before it; reopening a month also reopens the months after it. Both are kept in the change history.
locks.yearHint: Close the year after filing your tax return, and the books can't be changed. Reopen it if you need to fix something.

receivedBills.title: Received bills
receivedBills.description: Track payment due dates and status. Record payments separately on the Transactions screen.

documents.choosePaymentAccount: Choose the account that received the payment
documents.createDescription: Choose the document to make. You can save a draft and issue it later.
documents.empty: No documents yet. Use the buttons above to make one.
documents.taxNote: The format follows the year's consumption-tax setting (qualified invoices in taxable years). Documents are printed in Japanese. Check with a tax accountant that the contents are sufficient and how to keep copies of documents sent by email.
documents.partnerHint: Choosing one fills in the name, address and email.
documents.recipientNameHint: Include honorifics such as 御中 or 様.
documents.subject: Subject
documents.linesHint: Enter unit prices before tax. Enter discounts like "-1000". Quantities can have decimals such as 1.5.
documents.issueHint: Issuing gives the document a number and stores a PDF copy with your books. Issued documents can't be changed.
documents.issueConfirm: Once issued, the document can't be changed. Issue it?
documents.previewStale: The latest changes aren't shown yet.
documents.cancelConfirm: Cancel this document? If its sale was recorded, that transaction is deleted too. The canceled document is kept as a copy.
documents.webmailHint: The selected webmail service receives the recipient, subject and message. Attach the saved PDF in your email.
documents.mailAppOpened: The PDF was saved, and the draft and PDF folder were opened. Attach the PDF and send the email, then press "Mark as sent".
documents.saleHint: This entry will be recorded. Check it, then press "Record".
documents.linesHintNoTax: Documents with this issue date use the format without a registration number, so no consumption tax is added. Enter unit prices as the amounts you will receive. Enter discounts like "-1000". Quantities can have decimals such as 1.5.
documents.previewEmpty: Enter an item name to see the page here.

documentSettings.title: Invoices and other documents
documentSettings.description: Contact details, bank details, notes, logo and seal printed on documents, and the email template.
documentSettings.profileNote: Trade name, name, address and registration number come from your business details.
documentSettings.bankAccountHint: Printed on invoices. Example: Bank, branch, account type, number, account name
documentSettings.imagesHint: PNG or JPEG (up to 2 MB). The logo goes above your details, the seal to their right.
documentSettings.mailTemplateHint: Use this template for invoices, estimates, delivery notes and receipts. The buttons below each field insert at the cursor. Payment deadline is inserted only for invoices with a due date.
documentSettings.guidanceExamples: Show the sentence for each document type

mailSettings.title: Sending email
mailSettings.description: Settings for sending invoices and other documents directly from the app. Without them you can still send with "Open draft".
mailSettings.guideGmail: For Gmail, create an "app password" instead of using your usual password.
mailSettings.step1: Turn on 2-Step Verification for your Google account (needed to create app passwords).
mailSettings.step2: Open this page in your browser and create an app password (any name you'll recognize, such as "Chobiyori").
mailSettings.step3: Copy the 16 characters shown and paste them into "Password" below. Spaces are fine.
mailSettings.guideOther: For other email, enter the outgoing (SMTP) server name, port and encryption from your provider's guide, and your password. Some services don't accept sending from apps.
mailSettings.noteStored: The password is stored in this computer's keychain (credential store). It isn't kept in your books or shown on screen.
mailSettings.noteSentFolder: Sent emails also stay in your email service's Sent folder (depending on the service). The app records when and to whom you sent.
mailSettings.noteLeak: If the password may have leaked, delete that app password in your Google account (or service) and make a new one.
mailSettings.noteFallback: If sending fails, use "Open draft" on the document to send from your usual mail app.
mailSettings.fromNameHint: Shown in the recipient's mail app, such as your trade name.
mailSettings.usernameHint: If empty, the email address is used.
mailSettings.passwordHint: For Gmail, paste the app password. It isn't shown after saving.

filing.accountantNote: Check the NTA form and guide for the filing year for field locations, special rules and deadlines.
filing.incomeIntro: These are the values to enter on the National Tax Agency's return preparation site, in the order the site asks for them. Copy each value and paste it in.
filing.statementIssues: Issues in the statement figures: {count}. Fix them first on the Statement figures tab.
filing.section_plHint: Enter these on the profit and loss screen of the statement. Subtotals and totals are calculated by the site; just check they match.
filing.section_monthlyHint: The monthly boxes on page 2 of the statement.
filing.section_depreciationHint: For each asset, the amount counted as this year's expense. Details are on the Fixed assets tab.
filing.section_bsHint: Year-end balances. Needed for the 650,000- and 550,000-yen deductions.
filing.section_returnHint: After you enter the statement, the site fills in the business income on the return. Check that it matches.
filing.notInApp: Deductions (social insurance, life insurance, medical costs, dependents and so on), other income such as salary, and the tax itself are not calculated in this app. Enter them on the filing site.
filing.consumptionNotTaxable: No consumption tax return is needed for this year (tax-exempt). After registering for invoices, enter the registration number and date under Settings > Invoice registration.
filing.consumptionIntro: Sales by tax rate and estimated consumption tax based on the recorded tax categories.
filing.midYearNote: You registered partway through the year, so only transactions from {date} are counted.
filing.salesHint: From tax-included sales, the tax base (rounded down to 1,000 yen) and tax for each rate.
filing.special30Hint: Eligible sole proprietors may pay 30% of the consumption tax on sales for the 2027 and 2028 tax years.
filing.special20Hint: For people who became taxable by registering for invoices. You pay 20% of the consumption tax on sales. Check the years and conditions.
filing.special20NotPeriod: This year is outside the period of the 20% special rule.
filing.simplifiedHint: Calculated with the deemed purchase rate of each business category. A notification must be filed in advance.
filing.needsCategory: Some sales have no business category. Choose a business category.
filing.methodsChoose: Check the conditions and decide which method to file with. The standard method is an estimate.
filing.defaultCategoryHint: Your usual business category. It can be changed per sales account.
filing.cornerHint: The main values to enter on the consumption tax screens of the filing site.
filing.standardTitle: Totals by tax category (for the standard method)
filing.standardHint: To file with the standard method, give these totals to a tax accountant.
filing.checkDigitWrong: The number may not be in the right form. Check it again.
filing.openSiteHint: The number was copied. Paste it into the search on the public site, then press the button for the result.
filing.partnerChecksDescription: Check on the National Tax Agency's public site that each registration number is really registered. Nothing is sent from the app.
filing.partnerChecksEmpty: No partners have a registration number yet.
filing.partnerChecksWaiting: Partners not checked yet, or last checked over a year ago: {count}
filing.registrationDescription: Help with applying to register as a qualified invoice issuer. Once registered, enter the registration number and date.
filing.applyTitle: What to write on the application
filing.applyIntro: The main items for the application, taken from your business details. You can copy them.
filing.applyDateHint: If you are tax-exempt and register partway through a year, you can write the date you want to be registered from. Check the rules for the date in the National Tax Agency's guidance.
filing.applyStepEtax: By e-Tax: log in to e-Tax with your My Number card, choose the application for qualified invoice issuer registration and fill it in.
filing.applyStepMail: By post: print the form from the National Tax Agency's site, fill it in and send it to the invoice registration center for your area.
filing.applyStepWait: Once registered, you receive a notice with your registration number (electronically if you used e-Tax).
filing.afterReturn: A consumption tax return and payment are needed every year.
filing.afterSpecial20: If registering made you taxable, you may qualify for a temporary special measure.
filing.afterSimplified: To use the simplified method, a notification must be filed in advance.
filing.afterBooks: In this app, transactions from the registration date get tax categories, and invoices use the qualified invoice format.
filing.enterTitle: Enter the registration number and date
filing.registeredOnHint: The registration date written on the notice.
filing.methodHint: The calculation method for your {year} return. When you add or change the registration date, this method also applies to open tax-exempt years from the registration year onward.
filing.wasExempt: I was exempt before registering for invoices in this tax year
filing.midYearHint: Totals start on the registration date if registration made you taxable, and on January 1 if you were already taxable.
filing.reminderDay1: The day before and the due date
filing.reminderTimingHint: For example, with the 7-day reminder on, you’ll also see it if you open your books with 5 days left. Uncheck all options to turn reminders off.
filing.calendarHint: Save upcoming unfiled tax deadlines to an .ics file. You can import it into Google Calendar or Apple Calendar. Imported events are not synced with Chobiyori.
filing.calendarAlerts: Set alerts in your calendar app.
filing.calendarSaved: File saved. Import it into your calendar.
filing.calendarEmpty: There are no upcoming unfiled deadlines to export.
filing.reminderDesktopTiming: On Windows and Mac, opening your books schedules notifications for 9 a.m. local time on the selected days.
filing.reminderDesktopHint: Pick from 30, 7, or 1 day before the deadline. Scheduled notifications arrive even if Chobiyori is closed. On other days, opening your books also sends a desktop notification for each on-screen reminder, once per deadline per day.
filing.reminderScheduleFailed: The operating system could not schedule the notifications. Check notification settings and retry, or export the deadlines to your calendar.
filing.reminderScheduleUnavailable: Scheduled notifications are unavailable here. Allow notifications for the installed Windows or Mac app.
filing.deadlinesDescription: A deadline is coming up. Check your progress in the checklist on the Year-end screen.
filing.deadlinesCheck: Deadlines move for weekends and holidays. Check the National Tax Agency's guidance.
filing.check_statement_checkedHint: Check for issues on the Statement figures tab.
filing.check_my_number_card: Have your My Number card ready
filing.check_my_number_cardHint: To file with e-Tax you need the card and a smartphone or reader that can read it.
filing.check_deduction_certificatesHint: Papers showing what you paid for pension, health insurance, life insurance, medical costs and so on.
filing.check_corner_business: Entered the statement in the filing site
filing.check_corner_businessHint: Enter the values on this page into the statement screens of the filing site.
filing.check_corner_deductions: Entered deductions and other income in the filing site
filing.check_corner_deductionsHint: Deductions, other income such as salary, and the tax are entered and calculated on the filing site.
filing.check_submittedHint: File by e-Tax, by post, or at the tax office.
filing.check_paidHint: Pay by bank transfer, online banking, convenience store or at the office. The deadline is the same as filing.
filing.check_consumption_method: Chose how to calculate consumption tax
filing.check_consumption_methodHint: The 20% special rule or the simplified method (for the standard method, ask a tax accountant). Compare the amounts below.
filing.check_consumption_corner: Entered consumption tax in the filing site
filing.check_consumption_cornerHint: Enter the values on this page into the consumption tax screens of the filing site.
filing.check_consumption_submittedHint: It doesn't have to be filed together with the income tax return.
filing.check_consumption_paidHint: The deadline is the same as the consumption tax return.
filing.standardEstimateHint: An estimate that deducts the tax on purchases and expenses. Purchases without a qualified invoice deduct only the transitional share (80%, 70%, 50%, or 30%). Cases such as a taxable sales ratio below 95% are not calculated. Confirm with a tax accountant before filing.
filing.whiteIntro: Amounts for the white-return income and expense statement. Select white return in the NTA filing site and copy each amount. The family worker deduction is the amount saved in closing. See NTA No.2075 and the closing screen for eligibility and calculation.
filing.deductionTransferMode: Blue-return deduction to use for these figures
filing.deductionTransferHint: Choose 550,000 yen when it applies, for example when filing on paper without qualifying electronic books. Check the rules for your filing year.
filing.reminderScheduling: Checking notification reservations with the operating system.
filing.reminderScheduleEmpty: No notifications are scheduled. Check the unfiled deadlines and selected reminder days.
filing.reminderScheduleDenied: Notifications for Chobiyori are blocked. Allow them in the system notification settings, then retry.
filing.calendarSyncHint: A dedicated 帳日和 / Chobiyori calendar is created in Google Calendar or Outlook. Events include the type and date. Names and amounts stay in the app. Existing events remain when you pause sync or disconnect.
filing.calendarSchedulesHint: Upcoming deadlines for unfiled income and consumption tax returns are synced. Choose other events to add from today onward. Add payment due dates under Invoices → Received bills.
filing.calendarSchedule_invoiceDue: Payment due dates for issued invoices
filing.calendarSchedule_receivedBillDue: Payment due dates for received bills
filing.calendarCloseDayHint: Reminders fall in the following month. If the selected day is unavailable, the reminder falls on the last day of that month.
filing.calendarSyncPaused: Sync is off. Your connection and existing events are kept.
filing.calendarAuthorizing: Allow calendar access in your browser, then return to Chobiyori.

receivables.monthlyHint: Recurring sales due this month and the payments recorded. Recording a payment posts "account / sales".
receivables.noPlansThisMonth: No recurring sales are due this month. Add them under Recurring plans.
receivables.unpaidCount: Partners who have not paid in full: {count}
receivables.bulkHint: Recording them together records the missing amount for each. If an amount differs, use Record payment on that row.
receivables.asRefund: Record as a refund (subtracted from sales)
receivables.unassignedHint: Payments received without deciding whose or which month. They are recorded as sales and listed here separately.
receivables.yearHint: The payment status of each plan by month. Unpaid and partly paid months stand out.
receivables.legend: ○ paid　△ partly paid　× unpaid　– skipped　＋ unexpected payment
receivables.plansHint: Register fixed monthly sales such as tuition, membership or retainer fees per partner. When one ends, set its end month.
receivables.inUseHint: A plan with recorded payments can't be deleted. Set its end month instead.
receivables.noCustomers: There are no partners. Add one on the Master data screen.
receivables.draftInvoicesHint: Makes one draft invoice per partner from the recurring sales of the chosen month. Check them on the documents screen before issuing. Invoices for the same month are never made twice.
receivables.draftInvoicesDone: Drafts made: {count}. Skipped (already invoiced): {invoiced}. Skipped (already paid): {paid}.

deposits.saleNotRecorded: (issue the invoice first to record the sale)
deposits.linkHint: If this is a payment for an invoice or a recurring sale, choose it to record it as "bank / accounts receivable" or as the sale. Otherwise choose an account as usual.

tutorial.profileAction2: Check the trade name and save any changes
tutorial.profileAction3: Check the fiscal year in the sidebar
tutorial.entryAction2: Enter the expense date and amount
tutorial.ledgerAction3: Match the date and amount to the receipt
tutorial.reviewAction2: Compare a candidate with the journal
tutorial.reviewAction3: Confirm a new item or link an existing entry
tutorial.monthAction2: Compare the balance with your statement
tutorial.monthAction3: Check entries if the balances differ
tutorial.prepareAction1: Choose the last day in the old app
tutorial.prepareAction2: Save the journal and trial balance
tutorial.prepareAction3: Gather the balances for the move
tutorial.openingAction2: Match the opening balance for each account
tutorial.importAction1: Match counts and totals to the old books
tutorial.compareAction1: Select the same period as the old books
tutorial.compareAction3: Check balances and entries for differences
tutorial.backupAction3: Find the new backup in the list
tutorial.title: Guided walkthroughs
tutorial.profile: Check your business and fiscal year
tutorial.profileBody: Check your business details in Settings and the fiscal year in the sidebar. Have a receipt handy for the next step.
tutorial.entry: Enter an expense from a receipt
tutorial.entryBody: In Simple entry, select Expense. For stationery bought with cash, choose Supplies and Cash. Record the actual date and amount. If you have no unrecorded expenses, look over the fields and continue.
tutorial.ledger: Find the entry in your books
tutorial.ledgerBody: Open the journal for the month of the transaction and compare its date, amount and account with the receipt. If it is missing, check the year and date range.
tutorial.reviewBody: Open the pending list. For a new item, check its date, amount and account before confirming it. Link an item you already recorded to the existing transaction. If the list is empty, continue.
tutorial.monthBody: Select the month and compare the account balance with the bank statement at that month-end. If they differ, check the ledger by date for missing or duplicate entries.
tutorial.prepare: Choose a cutover date and save your old books
tutorial.prepareBody: Choose the last date you will record in your old app. Save its journal and trial balance. For a midyear move, gather opening balances and entries from the start of the year through cutover. For a new-year move, start from the previous year-end balances.
tutorial.openingBody: In Opening balances, check cash, deposits, receivables and loans against the old opening balances and confirm them once they match. Use the start-of-year amounts even for a midyear move.
tutorial.previewBody: Under Import books, choose Journal CSV. Match the columns and account codes to a journal CSV exported by this app. For a supported monthly Excel workbook, choose Excel and check the year and account mapping. Continue if you have no entries to transfer.
tutorial.importBody: Compare the preview year, entry count, skipped items and debit and credit totals with the old books. Fix flagged rows and select the file again. Once the figures match, import and check the result count. Continue directly if you only transferred opening balances.
tutorial.compareBody: Choose the same year and months as in the old app and compare each account on the trial balances. For differences, check opening balances, account codes, dates and duplicates. Once reconciled, record transactions after cutover in this app.
tutorial.backupBody: Check the destination under Backup and restore and choose Back up now. Confirm the new backup appears in the list. To restore it, use the book password from the time it was created.
tutorial.hideFromHomeNote: You can start a walkthrough from Help at any time.

help.profileStep: Check your name and trade name under Business details. Select Save if you make a change.
help.openSales: Enter a sale in Quick entry
help.salesStep: Select Income and choose the sales account under “What the income is for”. Check the date, amount and receiving account, then select Record.
help.personalExpenseStep: Select Expense. Under “Where it was paid from”, choose “I paid with personal funds or a personal card”.
help.receiptStep: Select Choose images to add a receipt photo. After reading it, check the date and amount under To review.
help.screen_closingStep: Find the first unfinished item on the checklist and work through that task.
help.allocationStep: Select Add, enter a name and the business-use percentage, then save the rule. Under Accounts, assign it to the account that uses the split.
help.exampleStep: Check the accounts, enter the actual date and amount, then select Record.
help.screen_homeStep: Under Account balances, compare the cash and bank balances with your cash on hand and bank statement.
help.screen_transactionsStep: In Quick entry, select Income for a sale or Expense for a payment, then enter its date and amount.
help.screen_inboxStep: Choose an item under To review and check its date, amount and account. If the list is empty, import a receipt or statement.
help.screen_ledgersStep: Select Journal to see transactions by date. Use From and To to choose the months to show.
help.screen_reportsStep: Select the end month and compare the bank balance under Account balances with your statement for that month.
help.screen_receivablesStep: Choose the month under Monthly payments. For a new recurring sale, enter the customer and monthly amount under Recurring plans.
help.screen_documentsStep: Under Create a document, choose a document type, enter the recipient and line items, then select Save draft.
help.screen_masterStep: Choose Accounts or Partners at the top. Select Add to create a new entry.
help.screen_dataStep: To import books, select Choose a file under Excel or CSV, then check the fiscal year and entry count in the preview.
help.screen_settingsStep: Choose the language or theme under Appearance. To change your name or trade name, open Business and accounting.
help.startBody: Set up your business, filing type, accounts and opening balances first. Record money coming in and out in Transactions. Once a month, compare your books with cash and bank statements.
help.salesBody: Record sales under Transactions > Quick entry > Income. If the customer has not paid yet, choose "The customer has not paid yet". For invoices made in Chobiyori, record the sale and payments from the issued invoice.
help.receiptBody: Add receipts in the Inbox, then check the date, amount and account that were read before recording them. Reading receipts needs an internet connection.
help.closingBody: Use the checklist on the Year-end closing screen to go through opening balances, fixed assets and inventory. Check the statement figures and the filing guide, then copy them into the National Tax Agency's filing site.
help.suppliesBody: Expense / Supplies / Cash. For ¥1,200, debit Supplies and credit Cash. Enter the actual date and amount.
help.cashSalesBody: Income / Sales / Cash. For ¥5,000, debit Cash and credit Sales.
help.journalBody: A record of a transaction using accounts and amounts.
help.debitBody: The left side of an entry. Used for increases in assets and expenses, among other things.
help.creditBody: The right side of an entry. Used for increases in revenue and liabilities. Both sides must total the same amount.
help.accountBody: A category such as Cash, Sales or Supplies that organizes transactions.
help.drawBody: Money taken from the business for personal use.
help.contributionBody: Personal money put into the business or used to pay business expenses.
help.allocationBody: Separate expenses shared between business and private use, such as home rent. Deduct only the business portion supported by records of floor area or usage time.
help.depreciationBody: Recording the cost of equipment over the period it is used.
help.capitalBody: The difference between business assets and liabilities at startup, among other adjustments.
help.keysBody: Ctrl+K (⌘K on Mac): command palette. F1: help for the current screen. Tab / Shift+Tab: next / previous control. Enter: activate. Esc: close palette. ↑ / ↓: select a result.
help.note: Check expense rules, business-use allocation and deduction eligibility against NTA public guidance and your records.
help.screen_homeBody: See this month's figures and what to do next.
help.screen_transactionsBody: Record sales and payments. Switch between quick entry, the journal grid and compound entries; all of them produce the same journal entries.
help.screen_inboxBody: Review candidates made from receipt photos and card or bank statements, and record them. Nothing goes into your books until you record it.
help.screen_ledgersBody: View the journal, general ledger, cash and bank books, expense book, and receivables and payables by partner, and save them as CSV or PDF.
help.screen_reportsBody: See the trial balance and account balances. Every figure is calculated from your journal entries.
help.screen_receivablesBody: Manage recurring sales such as tuition and membership fees, and their payments.
help.screen_closingBody: Finish opening balances, depreciation and inventory, and get the figures for the blue-return statement. This is also where you find the values for your income and consumption tax returns, and carry balances forward to the next year.
help.screen_masterBody: Manage accounts, descriptions, partners and business-use split rules.
help.screen_dataBody: Back up and restore your books, bring in books from Excel or CSV, save them as CSV or PDF, and see the change history.
help.screen_settingsBody: Use the descriptions under the headings to find a setting. For payment details on documents, open Documents and email. For filing reminders, open Business details and tax filing.
help.screen_helpBody: How to use the app and what the accounting terms mean, for first-time users.
help.screen_documentsBody: Create invoices, estimates, delivery notes and receipts, and send them as PDF or by email. Invoices connect to recording sales and payments.
help.missingExampleAccounts: This example’s accounts cannot be used. Check that the accounts are active and the payment account is enabled in Master.
help.sharedExpenses: Split a shared business and personal expense
help.sharedExpensesBody: In Master data > Business-use split rules, register a business share based on records such as floor area or usage time, and set it on the account. In Quick entry, enter the full amount you paid. The preset shares are examples, not rates you can always deduct. See NTA No.2210.
help.teachingMaterialsBody: Expense / Teaching materials / Cash. For ¥3,000, debit Teaching materials and credit Cash. Uses the school template’s accounts.
help.tuition: Receive monthly tuition by bank transfer
help.tuitionBody: Income / Sales / Ordinary deposits. Debit Ordinary deposits and credit Sales. If you have a recurring plan, also choose the plan and month under "Link a payment" in Quick entry.
help.referenceBooks: Buy reference books for work with cash
help.referenceBooksBody: Expense / Books and subscriptions / Cash. For ¥2,000, debit Books and subscriptions and credit Cash. Uses the service and freelance template’s accounts.
help.stockPurchase: Purchase goods for sale with cash
help.stockPurchaseBody: Expense / Purchases / Cash. Debit Purchases and credit Cash. Enter the value of goods left at year end under Year-end closing > Inventory.
help.restaurantSanitation: Pay for kitchen cleaning in cash
help.restaurantSanitationBody: Expense / Sanitation / Cash. Debit Sanitation and credit Cash.
help.constructionToolRental: Rent tools for a job and pay in cash
help.constructionToolRentalBody: Expense / Tool rental / Cash. Debit Tool rental and credit Cash.
help.beautySupplies: Buy hair color for salon treatments with cash
help.beautySuppliesBody: Expense / Treatment supplies / Cash. Debit Treatment supplies and credit Cash.
help.webHosting: Pay a Japanese web hosting provider by bank transfer
help.webHostingBody: Expense / Hosting and domain fees / Ordinary deposits. Debit Hosting and domain fees and credit Ordinary deposits.
help.deliveryToll: Pay a road toll in cash while making a delivery
help.deliveryTollBody: Expense / Road tolls / Cash. Debit Road tolls and credit Cash.
help.collectReceivable: Collect a sale previously recorded as receivable
help.collectReceivableBody: Income / Accounts receivable / Ordinary deposits. Debit Ordinary deposits and credit Accounts receivable. The sale is already recorded, so don't choose Sales again. For an invoice payment, also choose the invoice under "Link a payment" in Quick entry.
help.personalExpense: I paid a business expense with personal funds
help.personalExpenseBody: Under Transactions > Quick entry > Expense, choose "I paid with personal funds or a personal card" as where it was paid from. Enter what it was spent on and the amount; it is recorded against owner's contributions.

setupMore.opening: Opening balances and starting a business
setupMore.openingHint: Enter each account’s starting balance. If you have loans or other balances, you can add them below.
setupMore.firstYear: About start-up costs (for your first business year)
setupMore.startupHint: Special expenses for preparing to start a business may qualify as startup costs. Distinguish asset purchases and prepaid expenses. Record startup costs as an asset and post the amortization expense in the chosen year; amortization is not automatic. Discretionary amortization is limited to the unamortized balance. Keep spending and amortization records. Opening capital is opening assets minus liabilities.
setupMore.featuresHint: Unused features are hidden from menus. Saved records remain and you can re-enable features in Settings.
setupMore.additionalBalances: Enter other opening balances, such as loans
setupMore.featuresLater: You can change these later under Settings → Menus and fields shown in your books.
setupMore.screens_inventory: Turn on to show Inventory in Year-end closing.
setupMore.screens_receivables: Turn on to show Invoices in the sidebar, receivables and payables in Ledgers, and “Link a payment” in Quick entry.
setupMore.screens_recurring: Turn on to show Recurring sales in the sidebar and Monthly entries in Transactions.
setupMore.screens_allocation: Turn on to show business-use split rules in Master data and the split field in Quick entry.
setupMore.balanceInvalid: Enter the balance as a whole number (negative amounts are allowed).
